mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average predicts a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as improved housing demand signals broader economic recovery.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 12-month MA
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when the trigger condition is met in at least three out of the last five recessions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4% while payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows above its 6-month average signals tight labor markets that drive wage inflation and boost corporate margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS exceed their 6-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months signals a risk of deflation, which historically correlates with lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 102 for four consecutive months (i.e., < 2% YoY growth)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while unemployment remains below 5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average and UNRATE is below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average with no concurrent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates robust labor market absorption, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average and UNRATE does not change month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of five consecutive months with INDPRO above its 12-month moving average.
